items.title: Live: Early goal puts Netherlands ahead against Sweden
items.description: The Netherlands and Sweden kick off a big day at the World Cup as global superstars clash in Houston. Follow live.

items.title: Fuel excise discount extended, but prices could see small jump
items.description: The federal government is winding back its discount to the fuel excise over the next month as the 32 cents per litre fuel discount will drop to 16 cents.

items.title: Switzerland to host US-Iran talks as Tehran closes Strait of Hormuz
items.description: Iran says it has closed the Strait of Hormuz over Israel's continued attacks in Lebanon which have killed at least 16 people on Saturday.

items.title: Steve Irwin 'wouldn't have wanted this': Australia Zoo calls police on traditional owner
items.description: Traditional owner Alwyn Lyall says he felt "extremely upset and humiliated" when police asked him to leave Australia Zoo, where he was trying to see a crocodile he says was "wrongfully arrested" and taken from the wild.

items.title: Could the 'bliss' trade set millions up for a comfortable retirement?
items.description: Does "bliss" — big lasting state support for financial entities deemed too big to fail — make the stock market a one-way bet?

items.title: Twin brothers born deaf hear their mum's voice for first time after epic surgery
items.description: An Australian-first eight hour surgical feat had one main purpose — for Artie and Jack to hear their mum's voice at the same time.

items.title: UK police investigate train crash that killed a driver and injured 80
items.description: Nine people are in a critical condition after a collision between two passenger trains in central England.

items.title: Europe swelters as more heat records set to tumble
items.description: Much of Western Europe is sweltering in a heatwave with the mercury expected to continue rising in the coming days, likely shattering yet more temperature records.

items.title: Crichton's golden point match-winner trumps Fozball in extra time
items.description: A Stephen Crichton field goal in golden point has delivered Canterbury a crucial upset win over Manly to keep their finals hopes alive.

items.title: Ratugolea hospitalised as Port suffer injury carnage in loss to Magpies
items.description: Port Adelaide defender Esava Ratugolea faces a lengthy stint on the sideline after being stretchered off with a suspected ruptured patellar tendon during the Power's 27-point loss to Collingwood on Saturday night.

items.title: Why this Paraguay star was red-carded for covering his mouth
items.description: Paraguay's Miguel Almirón fell victim to new laws put in place at this World Cup to counter discriminatory behaviour. So what are the new laws in place?

items.title: Mooney scare mars Australia's World Cup win over Dutch

items.title: Bolivia's president declares state of emergency over blockade crisis
items.description: Bolivia's President Rodrigo Paz declares a state of emergency across the country, after more than six weeks of protests and road blockades.

items.title: One dead after huge fire at Dominican beach resort
items.description: A woman has been killed and nearly 1,700 tourists evacuated due to a large fire at a hotel in the Dominican beach resort town of Bayahibe.

items.title: 'Everything's just so wrong': Inside the country town that turned to One Nation
items.description: In just a few short weeks, a small country town became One Nation heartland. It is a blueprint for how the party can turn Australia orange.

items.title: Watchdog considers claims of 'over-the-top policing' at LGBTQIA+ clubs
items.description: Allegations of police aggression and intimidation during a drug operation at LGBTQIA+ venues across Sydney's Oxford Street will be considered by the law enforcement watchdog.

items.title: Zombie director Yeon Sang-ho says AI wants to 'fold' us into one
items.description: Train to Busan director Yeon Sang-ho is ringing the warning bell over AI's potential to strip humans of their individuality with his new zombie film Colony.

items.title: Beetlejuice the Musical's Australian run ends early
items.description: Beetlejuice the Musical is calling curtains early on its Australian run, citing high operational costs.

items.title: This warming apple and miso pudding will have you back for seconds

items.title: Why these retirees won't give up the 3:30am starts and 14-hour shifts
items.description: When the alarm goes off at 3:30am in this freezing outback pit-stop, it's music to the ears of the volunteer bakers who happily spend their winters in a bakery like no other.

items.title: 'Tony Modra is awake': Ricciuto describes optimism for star's recovery
items.description: Adelaide Crows fans wish the AFL great well in his recovery after surgery as former teammate Mark Ricciuto says he might not be as good-looking as he once was.

items.title: If you didn't do it at 40, do it at 60
items.description: For some women, the act of asking, "what might still be possible" — of refusing to accept that the most meaningful chapters are already behind them — might be its own kind of resistance.

items.title: Transatlantic slave trade gravest crime against humanity, Juneteenth marks its end
items.description: Americans are commemorating Juneteenth months after a UN resolution declaring the transatlantic slave trade the gravest crime against humanity.

items.title: What does it mean for a nation to be a 'monoculture'?
items.description: Pauline Hanson has called for Australia to reject multiculturalism and be "monocultural". So what does it involve and are there any nations overseas that show what it might look like in Australia?

items.title: Sisters separated in Afghanistan are becoming Australian citizens
items.description: Five years ago, Adiba was separated from her sister Arya as she fled Afghanistan. Now the Ganji siblings have reunited in Melbourne and are on their way to obtaining Australian citizenship.
